The in-class exercise of the statistics refresher, in three steps:

| Step | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Online quiz 1** on Canvas: five questions, alone, then compare with your neighbour | 3 + 2 minutes |
| 2 | **Coding exercise** in pairs: Tasks 1 to 5 below with the packages (polars, plotnine, scipy) | 15 minutes |
| 3 | **Posit Assistant**: the same tasks with the assistant; compare its code and numbers with yours (last section) | 10 minutes |

Then 5 minutes plenary. The kiosk from the slides kept a record for a whole year. Use the code of `stats_refresher.qmd` as a template, especially Step 6: the functions are the same, only the data are bigger. Write your answers as short sentences below each cell.

## The data

`data/kiosk/kiosk_year.csv`: 52 weeks, one row per week. The data are simulated for teaching.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `week` | 1 to 52; weeks 1 to 5 are the price test of the slides |
| `price` | price per bar, EUR: 3.00 regular, 2.50 in four promotion weeks |
| `units` | bars sold in the week |
| `temp` | average temperature of the week, °C |
| `display` | `yes` if a display stood next to the till |
| `rating` | median customer rating of the week, 1 to 5 stars |

This file sits in `sessions/01-foundations/`, so it reads the data two folders up (`../../data/...`). In the Positron console, run from the project folder, the path is `data/kiosk/kiosk_year.csv`.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs
from plotnine import aes, geom_point, ggplot, labs
from scipy import stats

kiosk = pl.read_csv("../../data/kiosk/kiosk_year.csv")
kiosk.head()
```
